Directions:In the question below, an argument is given, followed by three statements that either strengthen or weaken the given argument. From the options, choose the one that presents the correct relationship each statement bears with the given argument.

Note:- 'S' stands for strengthening statement, and 'W' stands for weakening statement.

Argument: The world will witness persistent food insecurity, biodiversity loss and degraded resources in the future if agrifood systems remain the same.

I. The extensive use of fertilisers and pesticides has led to the decline in soil fertility.

II. The current expansion in the use of genetically modified crops is helping us feed more people without expanding the land under agriculture.

III. The current practice of cultivating only a few popular varieties of crops, may lead to the extinction of other less popular crops that may help feed our increasing population.
questions.explanation: The argument tells us that if our agrifood systems are not changed, we will face food insecurity, biodiversity loss and degraded resources. I tells us how soil fertility is declining due to the use of fertilisers and will strengthen the argument. II tells us how the cultivation of genetically modified crops is helping meet the food requirements of our population. It will weaken the argument that current agricultural practices will lead to food insecurity. III tells us how current practices may lead to the extinction of some crop varieties which may help in feeding our increasing population. It will strengthen the given argument. Thus, A is the right answer.

What is the number of toys from box B01?

The box which contains 14 toys is kept third from the bottom. Two boxes are kept between the box which contains 14 toys and box B02. The vacant rack is neither above box B02 nor below the box which contains 14 toys.

That means, the box B02 is kept third from the top. The box adjacent to B02 is kept three places away from B03, which contains 21 toys.

But the number of toys from B03 is 21, thus the only possible number of toys from B04 = 27.  The number of toys from box B07 is a prime number. Thus, the number of toys from box B06 is 14. 

Again, we have:  The sum of the number of toys from box B07 and box B04 is twice the number of toys from box B05. Two boxes are kept between box B08 and box B01, which is kept immediately above the box which contains 27 toys. Box B05 is neither kept adjacent to the box which contains 23 toys nor B03. That means, in case (2) B01 is kept second from the bottom, case (1a) & case (1b) are not valid.

Case (1a) & case (1b) are not valid B05 is neither kept adjacent to the box which contains 23 toys nor B03.

questions.question: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to which of the following scientists?
options: Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson, and Omar M. Yaghi
Svante Pääbo, Carolyn Bertozzi, and Benjamin List
Akira Yoshino, Frances Arnold, and John B. Goodenough
Emmanuelle Charpentier, Jennifer Doudna, and Roger Penrose
questions.explanation:
• The correct answer is 'A' that is 'Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson, and Omar M. Yaghi'.
  • The 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was conferred upon Susumu Kitagawa (Japan), Richard Robson (Australia), and Omar M. Yaghi (US) for their pioneering work on metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) — crystalline materials composed of metal ions linked by organic molecules, creating large porous structures that allow the flow and storage of gases and chemicals.

Key Info: 

  • The trio—Kitagawa, Robson, and Yaghi—were recognized for creating metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), which are molecular structures with large spaces that allow gases and chemicals to move freely through them.
  • MOFs have wide-ranging applications in gas storage, catalysis, and drug delivery.
  • Omar M. Yaghi is not affiliated with Oxford University; he is a professor at the University of California, Berkeley, USA.
  • The other statements are correct — Kitagawa (Kyoto University), Robson (University of Melbourne), and Yaghi (UC Berkeley) shared the Nobel for their joint development of MOFs.

  • The three Nobel laureates represent three nations:

  1. Susumu Kitagawa – Japan (Kyoto University)
  2. Richard Robson – Australia (University of Melbourne)
  3. Omar M. Yaghi – United States (University of California, Berkeley)
  • As per Nobel Committee tradition, when multiple scientists share the award, the prize money is divided equally unless stated otherwise. Therefore, the 11 million Swedish kronor prize for 2025 is shared equally among Kitagawa, Robson, and Yaghi, honoring their collaborative work on MOFs.

questions.question: Linthoi Chanambam recently made history by winning India’s first-ever medal at which international sporting event?
questions.explanation:

questions.question: Who has recently taken charge as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)?
questions.explanation:

questions.question: Which institute secured the top position in both the Overall and Engineering categories in National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) 2025?
questions.explanation:

  • The Framework annually lists the top-performing universities, colleges, and institutes in India.

questions.question: Who is heading the committee formed to explore the creation of a domestic Big Four-like advisory firm in India?
questions.explanation:

  • The committee is led by Dipti Gaur Mukherjee, the Secretary of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), and is tasked with evaluating the possibility of creating an Indian firm that could match the scale and capabilities of the Big Four global consulting firms.

  • The meeting regarding the formation of an Indian Big Four-type firm was chaired by Shaktikanta Das, who serves as the Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister (not to be confused with the RBI Governor of the same name).
  • The officials named in the meeting include Ajay Seth (DEA Secretary), M Nagaraju (Financial Services Secretary), Arvind Shrivastava (Revenue Secretary), and Dipti Gaur Mukherjee (MCA Secretary). The Chief Economic Adviser was not mentioned as a participant.

questions.question: The Cabinet has approved a _______ grant-in-aid to the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) and enhanced the budget for PM Kisan Sampada Yojana by _____, taking its total outlay to ₹_______.
questions.explanation:

  • The Cabinet approved a ₹2,000 crore grant-in-aid to the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) to mobilize ₹20,000 crore for lending to cooperative societies over four years (2025-26 to 2028-29).

questions.question: Where was the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile production unit inaugurated by Rajnath Singh?
questions.explanation:

  • Defence Minister Rajnath Singh inaugurated the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile production unit in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: As per the passage, why does the author state that thoughts possess dynamic power that can take concrete shape?

questions.question:
How can we resolve to gather courage?

questions.question:
According to the passage, which of the following statement(s) is/are incorrect?

(I) One can derive inspiration from the examples of men who had shown tremendous courage even when being placed in extremely well situations.

(II)  They stood undaunted like a rock and never compromised with their principles.

(III) You can render yourself weak and helpless with your negative thoughts and, by the same token, you can make yourself strong and courageous by the use of powerful, positive thoughts.
questions.explanation:
Referring to the line of the second paragraph, ‘One can derive inspiration from the examples of men who had shown tremendous courage even when being placed in extremely adverse situations. 

Statement I is incorrect. As in the passage, extremely adverse situations are mentioned, not ‘extremely well situations’. 

Statement II  is correct. As in the passage, it is mentioned, ‘They stood undaunted like a rock and never compromised with their principles.’

Statement III is correct. As in the passage, it is mentioned, ‘You can render yourself weak and helpless with your negative thoughts and, by the same token, you can make yourself strong and courageous by the use of powerful, positive thoughts’.

Hence, option (A) is the most appropriate choice.

questions.question: Out of the following given options, which numbered paragraph talks about a great deal of the unhappiness in the world as per the information given in the paragraphs?

questions.question: What would be the appropriate word for the blank given in paragraph 3?
questions.explanation:

questions.question: The sentence given in (I) has four words given in bold. Amongst the given bold words, which of the following must be interchanged to make the sentence grammatically and contextually correct and meaningful?

questions.question: As given in the passage, which of the following words is the antonym of the word ‘fickleness’?
questions.explanation:
As given in the passage, the antonym of the word "fickleness" would be a word that represents stability, consistency, or steadfastness. Among the options provided, "normality" best represents these qualities.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct choice for the antonym of "fickleness" as per the passage.

Fickleness means changeability, especially as regards one's loyalties or affections.

questions.question:
How can we display courage?

(I) courage to earn one’s livelihood through fair means and not through corrupt practices

(II) courage to resist all sorts of temptations

(III) courage to adhere to the path of truth and righteousness

(IV) courage to be what one really is and not to have pretensions of being what one is not

questions.question:
Directions: In the following questions, a phrasal verb is given with its usage in the given sentences; you have to choose the option in which the usage of the phrasal verb is appropriate in the sentence.

Put off

A. The principal of the school has put the Parents-Teacher Meeting off and asked the teachers to prepare the progress report of the students as soon as possible.

B.The lawyer put off meeting his clients as he was discussing their case with a senior lawyer.

C. The doctor should not have put the patient off by telling him to wait, as he was in pain.

D. Tomorrow is my exam, so please don’t put me off my revision.
questions.explanation:
Put off : delay doing something /to make somebody wait / stop someone concentrating.  Here, ‘put off ’ is correctly used in all the sentences.

In the first sentence, it states that the principal of the school has delayed the Parents-Teacher Meeting and asked the teachers to prepare the progress report of the students as soon as possible. So here the usage of the phrasal verb is correct.

The second sentence tells us that the lawyer postponed or delayed the meetings, hence the usage of Put off is correct.

In the third sentence, the doctor should not have asked the patient to wait, as he was in pain. Here, the usage is correct.

In the fourth sentence, Tomorrow is my exam, so please don’t distract me as I am revising my lessons. So, the usage of phrasal verbs is correct.

So option A is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Directions: In the following questions, a phrasal verb is given with its usage in the given sentences; you have to choose the option in which the usage of phrasal verb is appropriate in the sentence.

Talk over

A. Event will be organized next month so we need to talk over the arrangements that are to be made.

B. My brother and I often talk over the expenses which we make as we want to reduce our expenses.

C. He is not an honest man and always gives you the wrong information, you should not talk him over.

D.Before hearing, the lawyer came to talk over the case as he got some important information.
questions.explanation:
Talk over: to discuss something. Here, ‘talk over’ is correctly used in the sentences A, B, and D.

In the first sentence, it states that the Event will be organized next month, so we need to discuss the arrangements that are to be made. So here the usage of the phrasal verb is correct.

The second sentence tells us that My brother and I often discuss the expenses that we make, as we want to reduce our expenses. So here, the word usage is appropriate.

In the third sentence, He is not an honest man and always gives you the wrong information; you should not trust him. Here, usage is incorrect.

In the fourth sentence, before the hearing, the lawyer came to discuss the case as he had gotten some important information. Here, the usage of phrasal verbs is correct.

So, option E is the correct answer.

questions.question:

questions.question:
Directions: In the following question, a statement is divided into five parts. Rearrange the parts to form a coherent and grammatically correct sentence. The first part of the sentence is given in bold to help you rearrange the other parts accordingly. Choose the best alternative among the five options given below each statement as your answer.

Simply floating in water as a/ optimal endocrine and organ functions (A)/regular practice can help you (B)/ build your mental calm and (C)/organise your body’s abilities for (D).
questions.explanation:
The given sentence starts with "Simply floating in water as a", which introduces the subject of the sentence. The rest of the sentence should logically connect to this idea in a grammatically and contextually correct manner.

  • (B) "regular practice can help you" follows naturally, as it explains how floating in water can be beneficial.
  • (C) "build your mental calm and" continues the thought, describing one of the benefits of this practice.
  • (D) "organise your body’s abilities for" adds further detail, explaining another advantage of floating in water.
  • (A) "optimal endocrine and organ functions" concludes the sentence by specifying the physiological benefits.

Thus, the correct order is BCDA, making Option B the right choice. The sentence conveys that regularly floating in water can enhance mental calmness and improve the body's physiological functions, emphasizing its holistic health benefits.

The final sentence is:

Simply floating in water as a regular practice can help you build your mental calm and organise your body’s abilities for optimal endocrine and organ functions.

questions.question: If the HCF and LCM of two numbers are 10 and 30 respectively and the sum of these numbers is 40, then find the sum of the reciprocals of these numbers.

HCF of a and b is 10, and the LCM of a and b is 30

\(\text{a } \times b\  = \ 10 \times 30\)

\(\text{a } \times b\  = \ 300\)

sum of the two numbers is \(40\)

\(a\  + \ b\  = \ 40\)

Therefore;

\(\frac{1}{a}\  + \ \frac{1}{b}\)

\(\frac{1}{a}\  + \ \frac{1}{b}\  = \ \frac{a\  + \ b}{\text{ab}}\)

\(\frac{40\ }{300} = \ \frac{4\ }{30} = \ \frac{2}{15}\)

Therefore, the sum of the reciprocals of a and b is \(\frac{2}{15}\).

questions.explanation:
According to the given data,

The total time taken in the journey by all the drivers together \(= 200\ hours\)

Now, the time taken by Sita \(= \frac{1}{8} \times 200 \Rightarrow 25\ hours\)

\(5x = 200 - 105\)

\(x = \frac{95}{5} \Rightarrow x = 19\)

Time taken by Shayam \(= 3 \times 19 \Rightarrow 57\ hours\)

The distance covered by Radha is 684 km.

As we know, \(speed = \frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}\)

Speed of Sita \(= \frac{300}{25} \Rightarrow 12\ kmph\)

Directions: Each of the questions below consists of a question and two statements numbered I and II given below it. You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and give answer:

Two trains running in opposite directions cross a pole on the platform in 54s and 34s respectively. Find the ratio of their speeds.

Statement I : Both the trains cross each other in 46 seconds running in opposite directions.

Statement II : The length of the two trains is in the ratio 34 : 81.
options: If the data in statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement II alone is not sufficient to answer the question
If the data in statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement I alone is not sufficient to answer the question
If data either in statement I alone or statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question
If data in both statements I & II together are necessary to answer the question
If data given in both I & II together are not sufficient to answer the question
questions.explanation:
Let the trains be A and B, their lengths be LA and LB and their speeds be SA and SB

LASA=54 and LBSB=34

LA = 54 × SA andLB= 34 × SB

Statement I : Both the trains cross each other in 46 seconds.

LA+LBSA+SB=46

LA + LB = 46(SA + SB)

Putting LA = 54 × SA and LB = 34 × SB

54SA + 34SB = 46SA + 46SB

8SA = 12SB

SA : SB = 3 : 2

So, statement I is alone sufficient

Statement II : The length of the two trains is in the ratio 34 : 81.

EitherLA : LB = 34 : 81 or LB : LA = 34 : 81

As we do not know which ratio is correct. So, statement II alone is not sufficient.

Directions: Each of the questions below consists of a question and two statements numbered I and II given below it. You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and give answer:

In a tank, A and C are inlet pipes and B is an outlet pipe. Pipes A and C can fill the tank in a certain time, but if pipe B is opened 40 minutes after both A and C are opened, it will take 21 minutes more to fill the whole tank than the time taken by A and C alone. In how much time pipes A and C together can fill the whole tank?

Statement I : A is thrice as efficient as C.

Statement II : B and C together are half as efficient as C alone.
options: If the data in statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement II alone is not sufficient to answer the question
If the data in statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement I alone is not sufficient to answer the question
If data in both statements I & II together are necessary to answer the question
If data either in statement I alone or statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question
If data given in both I & II together are not sufficient to answer the question
questions.explanation:
Efficiency of A = a, B = b and C = c

Let us say A and C together can fill the whole tank in 40+x minutes

After 40 minutes pipe B is also opened and it took 21 minutes more to fill the tank

(a + c) × x = (a + c + b)×(x + 21)

– b (x + 21) = (a + c) × 21

To find the value of x we need the efficiency of A, B and C

Statement I : A is thrice as efficient as C.

Statement II : B and C together are half as efficient as C alone.

Using either of the statements we cannot find the efficiency of all three

Using both the statements :

a = 3c

b+c=c2

b=-c2

a : b : c = 6 : – 1 : 2

– b (x + 21) = (a + c) × 21

1 × (x + 21) = (6 + 2) × 21

x = 147

Pipes A and C together can fill the whole tank in 40 + 147 = 187 minutes

So, both the statements are together necessary
